parts.text:
You read part of an interview. An analyst asked one future user of a software service a series of questions. You decide, for each question, whether it follows up the answer given just before it.

A question follows up the previous answer when it asks about something that answer said: it asks the speaker to explain, give an example of, say more about, or say why of something the answer mentioned, or it picks up a particular thing the answer named. Wording does not matter; a question can follow up an answer without repeating any of its words.

A question does not follow up the previous answer when it turns to something that answer did not mention, even if the speaker said it in an earlier answer, even if it stays with the same broad subject, and even if it is a good question. A general question that could follow any answer, such as whether there is anything else, does not follow up either.

You receive the pairs of the interview after its first question: for each later question, the answer given just before it, and the question.

Reply with JSON only: an object with one key, "questions", a list with exactly one entry for every pair, in the same order. Each entry has "id", the question's id, and "follow_up", true or false.

Q2
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: That's fine, let's make it smaller. Think of your most recent shift: what was the very first thing you did when you got in?

Q3
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: No problem. In your own words, what is your job as a dispatcher?

Q4
The answer just before it: As a dispatcher, I plan and run the flights as the licensed person responsible for each one. I decide which drone flies and along which way, and I sign off a flight before it leaves. I can also call off a flight.
The question: Take the last flight you signed off: what did you look at or do before you gave that sign-off?

Q5
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: That's okay. In general, what do you need to know before you sign off a flight?

Q6
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: You mentioned you can call off a flight. What kinds of things make you call one off?

Q7
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Let's try a different angle. Who gives you work, and who do you pass work on to?

Q8
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Understood. Has there been a day in the last few months that went badly for you at work, and if so, what happened?

Q9
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: That's fine. I notice my questions are proving hard to answer; what would make it easier for you to talk about your work?

Q10
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Okay. A new service is going to be built for dispatchers like you. What worries you about that?

Q11
The answer just before it: I worry because the service runs on a single server, and it is updated and restarted during working hours while drones are flying. It also occasionally crashes, although the companies accept a few minutes of interruption.
The question: When it restarts or crashes while your drones are in the air, what does that mean for you as the person responsible for those flights?

Q12
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: After the service comes back from an interruption like that, what do you need to know first?

Q13
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Is there anything in your work today that you double-check by hand because you don't trust what you're shown?

Q14
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Besides the restarts and crashes, what else worries you about a new service?

Q15
The answer just before it: I worry that management or analytical reports, exports, and dashboards beyond day-to-day operations might be included. I also worry if someone tries to log in through their own corporate identity systems, or uses several languages.
The question: Why would it worry you if reports, exports, and dashboards were included?

Q16
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: You said you sign off each flight before it leaves. What could a new service get wrong about that sign-off?

Q17
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: Is there anything else about a new service that worries you, beyond what you've already mentioned?

Q18
The answer just before it: I worry about any guarantee of meeting regulations, compliance audits, or data-retention and deletion features being included. I also worry about backups, high availability, or spreading the service over several servers. Finally, it worries me if accounts and passwords inside the service, weather information, or billing and pricing of the work are part of it.
The question: What do you rely on the fleet technicians for?

Q19
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: And what do you rely on the airspace desk for?

Q20
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: What must a new service never do, from your point of view?

Q21
The answer just before it: From my point of view, software must never choose a drone or a way for us to fly. I also worry if the service tries to send alerts to staff by e-mail, text message, or phone, or if anyone attempts to fly drones remotely through the service.
The question: Why must the choice of drone and way stay with you rather than with software?

Q22
The answer just before it: Choosing the drone and the way it flies is my legal responsibility as a dispatcher.
The question: What else are you legally responsible for as a dispatcher?

Q23
The answer just before it: As a dispatcher, I am the licensed person responsible for each flight, which includes deciding which drone flies and along which way, and signing off a flight before it leaves.
The question: And what must a new service always do for you, without fail?

Q24
The answer just before it: I don't know.
The question: After a crash or restart while drones are flying, what must the service never do?

Q26

Q27

Q28

The question: What information do you work with today that you don't fully trust?

Q29

Q30

The question: Other drone companies will be using this same service. What worries you about that?
